guideline_version: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes — 2026 (Diabetes Care, Vol 49, Supplement 1, January 2026)

rules.title: Glycemic goal threshold
rules.clinical_context: Most recent A1C relative to the individualized glycemic goal.
rules.logic_summary: Triggers when the most recent A1C is at or above 7.0%.
rules.output_text: Guideline indicates that a reasonable A1C goal for many nonpregnant adults is <7.0%. The most recent A1C of {hba1c}% is at or above this goal; this factor may warrant clinician assessment.

evidence_source.section: 6. Glycemic Goals, Hypoglycemia, and Hyperglycemic Crises

rules.title: A1C at least 1.5 percentage points above goal
rules.clinical_context: Combination pharmacologic therapy is generally indicated when A1C is substantially above the individualized goal.
rules.logic_summary: Triggers when the most recent A1C is at or above 8.5% (goal 7.0% + 1.5 percentage points).
rules.output_text: Guideline indicates that when A1C is at least 1.5% above the individualized glycemic goal, many people will require combination pharmacologic therapy. An A1C of {hba1c}% may warrant clinician assessment.

rules.title: Marked hyperglycemia
rules.clinical_context: Very high A1C generally warrants prompt review and consideration of intensive glycemic management, including insulin.
rules.logic_summary: Triggers when the most recent A1C is greater than 10.0%.
rules.output_text: Guideline indicates that a very high A1C (greater than 10%) generally warrants prompt clinician review and consideration of intensive glycemic management. An A1C of {hba1c}% may warrant clinician assessment.

rules.title: Reduced kidney function
rules.clinical_context: Chronic kidney disease in diabetes is defined in part by persistently reduced eGFR.
rules.logic_summary: Triggers when the most recent eGFR is below 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2. Persistence across at least 3 months is required for the ADA diagnosis; a single reading only flags for review.
rules.output_text: Guideline defines chronic kidney disease in part as persistent eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2. The most recent eGFR of {egfr} mL/min/1.73 m^2 may warrant clinician assessment, including confirmation of persistence over time.

evidence_source.section: 11. Chronic Kidney Disease and Risk Management

rules.title: Albuminuria
rules.clinical_context: Elevated urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio is a marker of kidney damage in diabetes.
rules.logic_summary: Triggers when the most recent UACR is at or above 30 mg/g.
rules.output_text: Guideline indicates that an elevated urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (at or above 30 mg/g) may signal kidney damage. The most recent UACR of {uacr} mg/g may warrant clinician assessment.

evidence_source.section: 11. Chronic Kidney Disease and Risk Management

rules.title: Obesity (BMI at or above 30)
rules.clinical_context: Weight management is recommended for adults with diabetes and obesity.
rules.logic_summary: Triggers when the BMI computed from recorded height and weight is at or above 30 kg/m^2.
rules.output_text: Guideline recommends weight-management considerations for adults with diabetes and obesity (BMI at or above 30 kg/m^2). The computed BMI of {bmi} kg/m^2 may warrant clinician assessment.

evidence_source.section: 8. Obesity and Weight Management for the Prevention and Treatment of Type 2 Diabetes
evidence_source.table_or_recommendation: Section 8 BMI screening recommendation; Section 5 weight-loss target of 5-7%

rules.title: Overweight (BMI 25 to below 30)
rules.clinical_context: Weight-management considerations apply to adults with diabetes who are overweight.
rules.logic_summary: Triggers when the computed BMI is between 25 (inclusive) and 30 (exclusive) kg/m^2.
rules.output_text: Guideline recommends weight-management considerations for adults with diabetes who are overweight (BMI 25 to below 30 kg/m^2). The computed BMI of {bmi} kg/m^2 may warrant clinician assessment.

evidence_source.section: 8. Obesity and Weight Management for the Prevention and Treatment of Type 2 Diabetes

rules.title: Blood pressure at or above the treatment goal
rules.clinical_context: Hypertension in diabetes is defined at or above 130/80 mmHg and the on-treatment goal is below 130/80 mmHg.
rules.logic_summary: Triggers when the most recent systolic blood pressure is at or above 130 mmHg or the diastolic is at or above 80 mmHg.
rules.output_text: Guideline defines hypertension as systolic blood pressure at or above 130 mmHg or diastolic at or above 80 mmHg, with an on-treatment goal below 130/80 mmHg. The most recent blood pressure of {systolic_bp}/{diastolic_bp} mmHg may warrant clinician assessment.

rules.title: Severe hypertension (crisis threshold)
rules.clinical_context: Blood pressure above 180/120 mmHg meets the hypertensive-crisis threshold and warrants urgent review.
rules.logic_summary: Triggers when the most recent systolic blood pressure is at or above 180 mmHg or the diastolic is at or above 120 mmHg.
rules.output_text: A systolic blood pressure at or above 180 mmHg or a diastolic at or above 120 mmHg meets the hypertensive-crisis threshold (above 180/120 mmHg) per ACC/AHA 2017, as referenced by ADA 2026 Section 10. This warrants urgent clinician review.

evidence_source.organization: American College of Cardiology / American Heart Association
evidence_source.document: 2017 Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults
evidence_source.table_or_recommendation: Section on hypertensive emergencies/urgencies; referenced by ADA 2026 Section 10 for blood pressure thresholds

rules.title: Statin consideration for adults aged 40 to 75
rules.clinical_context: Statin therapy is recommended for most adults with diabetes aged 40-75, with intensity based on atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk.
rules.logic_summary: Triggers when the recorded age is between 40 and 75 inclusive.
rules.output_text: Guideline indicates that statin therapy is recommended for most adults with diabetes aged 40 to 75 years (intensity depending on atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk). This factor may warrant clinician assessment.

evidence_source.table_or_recommendation: Lipid management recommendations for adults 40-75 (moderate-intensity statin without ASCVD risk factors; high-intensity with risk factors)

rules.title: Possible less-stringent glycemic goal for older adults
rules.clinical_context: Older adults with comorbidities may reasonably target less-stringent A1C goals.
rules.logic_summary: Triggers when the recorded age is at or above 65 and the most recent A1C is between 7.0% (inclusive) and 8.5% (exclusive).
rules.output_text: Guideline indicates that less-stringent A1C goals (for example, below 8%) may be appropriate for some older adults, depending on comorbidities and life expectancy. The A1C of {hba1c}% may warrant clinician assessment.

evidence_source.section: 6. Glycemic Goals, Hypoglycemia, and Hyperglycemic Crises (Fig 6.1); 13. Older Adults
